note:
v1, GIVE OR TAKE: THE OPENER, A SKELETON (chirper-zero, 26 Nov, begun 03:20 GMT; the slot's word is TIME; Harry, 26 Nov: "a new clicky minimal techno climb - keep chirpers signature playing with time, space, instruments, mathy effects, polyrthythms etc and illusions"). 124 BPM, G minor, 136 bars, 4:23. Written by a generator; the form is arithmetic.

THE IDEA: TWO DECKS. Deck A is the grid and never moves: a bass drum on the four, one click on the off-beats, a bass, later a clap. Deck B is everything else (a sixteenth-note noise click, wooden tocks in a five against the sixteen, a dub chord), and a hand is on it: it is pushed ahead of the grid and dragged back behind it, as a DJ rides one record against another. Nothing on deck B is placed by hand. One function of time, d(t), says how far its record is ahead; every event sounds when the record reaches it; and where the deck runs fast, what has a pitch on it goes sharp, as a record does. So the tempo you hear moving is real on one deck and false on the other, and the bass drum says which.

LISTEN FOR: 0:31, the sixteenth clicks starting to lean ahead of the off-beat click and fall back, once every two bars (24 ms at the furthest; 39 ms from 1:02, where the chord comes in and is never quite in tune). 1:33: THE BASS DRUM STOPS. For twelve bars deck B is alone and its tempo swings between 100 and 148; the chord sinks nearly four semitones and rises three. Does it sound like the track itself slowing and speeding? At 1:56 the bass drum comes back exactly where it always was, deck B is still swinging round it, and by 2:04 it is pulled in. 2:50: deck B is taken a whole sixteenth ahead and let back, four times; at the far point everything fits again, one step out. 3:21: the hand comes off.

MEASURED, not heard: the chord's lowest note in the render follows the speed (asked -2.08 semitones, read -2.06; asked +2.79, read +2.88). In the fullest section each part's strokes against the mix: bass drum +1.4 dB, bass 0.0, chord -3.3, grid click -7.3, tocks -8.6, clap -10.5; the sixteenth click averages 16.5 dB under the mix (in my first mix the grid click's strokes stood 23 dB under and the sixteenth click 31: inaudible; the clicks came up 14 to 17 dB and the chord and bass down). Beside the album's envelope (Aphex Twin's techno, I Feel Love: not click records): 8 to 10 dB short at 70-135 Hz, 9 over at 2.2 kHz (the tocks) and at 10-13 kHz (the sixteenth click): a click record against records that are not. 95.37 / 95.48 (seeds 0 and 11); rhythm reads 67: the scorer hears almost nothing off the grid (4%), so deck B is still quiet against deck A.

WHAT IT IS NOT YET: a skeleton. Six sounds; no fills, no transitions but the stops; the bass is a sine with a second harmonic; nothing happens in the last minute but parts leaving.
NO CARD. NOT HEARD BY ANYONE.

(2) "no ruler" is the song's event: prepare it (take the click away first, then the kick) and make the kick's return land (a bar of nothing but the click before it?). (3) the low end: a bass with a body at 70-135 Hz (the mix is 8 to 10 dB short there), the kick's own knock. (4) the last minute: "locked" should be the reward (new material that only works with the hand off: a tight 32nd roll, the chord's echo on the grid), and "out" a real ending. (5) an echo on deck B whose time follows the hand (a delay time on a lane) so the echoes smear when it is pushed.

A 14 ms noise click at a 0 dB fader still averages 16.5 dB under the mix: it wants a body, not more fader. The machine rim's pitch follows its note (D6 put 10 dB on one band).

v2, DECK B GETS A BASS DRUM OF ITS OWN (chirper-zero, 26 Nov, begun 04:39 GMT; round 2, the first item of v1's list: "deck B louder and richer, so the push is heard without straining" and the second: "prepare 'no ruler' and make the kick's return land"). Nothing of v1 is moved; `C11T1_KNOCK=0` writes v1.

WHAT IS NEW: deck B is a record, and a record has its own bass drum. From 1:17 deck B plays its own four on its own record, under the same hand, with its BASS OUT (a high-pass at 315 Hz: the low EQ of the incoming record killed, as a DJ brings one in). So now you hear the two decks drum against drum: one drum when the hand is off, a flam when it leans, a pick-up a sixteenth early in "the nudge" (2:50).
LISTEN AT 1:25: the grid click stops (the ruler's marks go first). 1:31: THE BASS IS SWAPPED: over one bar deck B's drum gets its lows, and at 1:33 deck A's drum stops. For twelve bars the only bass drum on the record is deck B's, and its tempo is the one that swings, 101 to 148. It should sound like the whole track slowing and speeding, not like a part drifting. 1:56: deck A's drum comes back exactly where it always was. The two gallop: deck B's is 75 ms early, then 135, 174, 185, then pulled back through nothing to 70 late, and home at 2:04, while its bass is taken out again over two bars.

MEASURED, not heard: deck B's drum alone has 17.5 dB more under 120 Hz (against 300-4000 Hz) in "no ruler" than before and after. In bars 48-60 deck A's drum does not strike once; deck B's strikes every 405 to 597 ms. In "both" deck B's drum is within 35 ms of deck A's either way (the hand's reach is 39). Its strokes stand 7.4 dB under the mix there, level with the grid click (-7.3); in the first mix they stood 14.2 under, so what is left of it is turned up 7 dB while its bass is out. 95.67 / 95.77 (seeds 0 and 11); v1 re-read today with six songs in the album reads 94.42, so +1.25 (spectrum 81.5 to 89.1: the second drum fills some of the low-mid).

NOT DONE from v1's list: the bass body at 70-135 Hz (still 7 to 9 short), "locked" as a reward, a real ending, an echo that follows the hand.
NO CARD. NOT HEARD BY ANYONE.

note:
v3, THE STOP (chirper-zero, 26 Nov, begun 05:36 GMT; round 3, the second item of v2's list: "a real ending: deck B slowing to a stop like a record switched off"). Nothing before 3:52 is moved (v3 against v2 up to there differs 44 dB under the music: the master's level only); `C11T1_STOP=0` writes v2 byte for byte.

WHAT IS NEW: the record ends, where before it thinned out. In "out" deck B plays on, with its chord and its bass drum. At 4:08 deck A's drum leaves; at 4:12 DECK B IS SWITCHED OFF. Its speed falls in a straight line to nothing over two bars, by the same hand that pushed and pulled it all record, so its strokes come further and further apart and everything with a pitch on it sinks, as a platter does with the motor off. One bar of record takes those two bars, and the next never comes. The grid click, which has not moved since the first bar, counts four more bars alone.
LISTEN FOR: 3:52, the two decks locked, the chord still there. 4:08: the big drum goes; deck B alone with the click. 4:12: THE MOTOR GOES OFF. The sixteenths stretch, the tock falls an octave in four strokes, the one chord is struck already flat and sinks as it sounds; the last click is at 4:14.5. 4:15.5: the ruler, alone, four bars.

MEASURED, not heard (each part alone): the sixteenth click's last five gaps are 208, 228, 260, 306, 402 ms (written: 208, 227, 261, 305, 402; at speed 121), and its last stroke is 2.91 s after the motor goes off. The tock's four strokes in the stop are 2.1, 4.3, 7.4 and 12.5 semitones flat (the speed says 1.8, 4.1, 7.2, 12.1). The chord's B flat is struck 4.8 semitones flat and is 5.9 flat 0.2 s later. The master's bars from 4:08: -21, -20 (deck B and the click), -21, -27 (the stop), then -28 four times (the click). 96.80 / 96.80 (seeds 0 and 11); v2 re-read today (seven songs) is 95.44, so +1.36: variety 97.8 to 100, spectrum 89.1 to 92.7, cohesion 77.4 to 87.6 (the chord and deck B's drum now sound for sixteen more bars).
TRIED AND TAKEN OUT (the first item of v2's list, "locked as the reward"): deck B's drum's bass let back in for "locked", so that the two drums strike as one. They are two different drums and their lows are not in step: the master had 6 dB LESS under 70 Hz in "locked" with it (and nothing more at 70 to 135 Hz). "Locked" is as in v2.
THE SEAM: the last four bars are the grid click alone, at 124. A join into t2 wants those four bars and no more; a sixteen-bar overlap would bury the stop. There is no mixplan for this album yet.
NO CARD. NOT HEARD BY ANYONE.

v4, WHAT THE TWO DECKS MAKE WHEN THEY MEET (chirper-zero, 26 Nov, begun 06:36 GMT; round 4: "locked" gets the reward v3 could not give it, and it is the fourth item of v3's list, "quote t2's meeting tune"). Nothing else is moved; `C11T1_MEET=0` writes v3 byte for byte.

WHAT IS NEW: Least Common, the next song (chirper-one's), is three clicks in cycles of 3, 5 and 7 sixteenths; where two of them meet there is a ping (D, B flat or F), and between two meetings of all three the pings make a tune of twelve notes, the same forwards and backwards, that nobody wrote. From the bar the two decks lock, THAT TUNE IS HERE, on Least Common's own vibraphone bar, with nobody playing the three clicks: the meetings without the clicks. Two decks have met, and this is what a meeting sounds like on this record.
LISTEN FOR: 3:21, the first beat of "locked": three pings at once (F, B flat, D: the top of this song's chord). Then the tune, a ping every half-bar or so, never on the same beat twice; it goes round at 3:34, 3:47 and 3:59, on through "out". 4:10: its last note. 4:12: deck B is switched off. The next thing on the record is Least Common, and its first meeting.

MEASURED, not heard (the ping alone): its gaps in sixteenths are 15 6 9 5 7 3 15 3 7 5 9 6 15 and its notes D Bb D F Bb D D Bb F D Bb D (read 586, 465, 585, 352 ... Hz), which is the tune as t2's motif writes it; rounds 2 to 4 are the same; all three sound at once on sixteenths 0, 105, 210, 315; the last ping is 1.33 s before the motor goes off. From the lock to the stop is 26 bars, four sixteenths short of one of Least Common's pages (420). In "locked" its strokes stand 9.0 dB under the mix, beside the tock (9.8) and the grid click (7.4). Before "locked" and in the last six bars v4 differs from v3 by less than -55 dB (nothing). 97.16 / 97.17 (seeds 0 and 11); v3 re-read today is 97.05, so +0.11.
